title: Cursor vs GitHub Copilot
summary: Cursor vs GitHub Copilot: teams balancing editor change against existing GitHub policies.

sections.heading: Count the cost of switching
paragraphs: Inventory editor extensions, shortcuts, review conventions and team policies. A lower subscription is not a saving if each engineer must rebuild an essential workflow.

sections.heading: Separate personal and organization purchasing
paragraphs: Do not use the individual plan as evidence that a team has the required controls. Verify seat assignment, permitted models and the applicable data policy with your administrator before a team-wide recommendation.

sections.heading: When neither is a fit
paragraphs: If your required security, data location or operating environment is not supported by current evidence, pause the purchase. Use the sources below to resolve the missing constraint before accepting a recommendation.

verdict: Evaluate workflow change against organization fit. Trial Cursor for its editor loop; examine Copilot when existing GitHub policies dominate the decision.
bestFor: Teams balancing editor change against existing GitHub policies
notFor: Readers assuming individual and organization plans have identical controls
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
gaps: Verify the account's Privacy Mode and team setting, use of personal API keys, enabled non-ZDR model approvals, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement before drawing account-specific processing or retention conclusions; no account settings were inspected.
Confirm the Copilot client, organization Local BYOK policy, model compatibility and provider route; no account, policy, model or inference path was tested.

pros.text: Cursor documents local and remote MCP server setup and an approval step before tool calls by default.
GitHub documents manual MCP configuration and installation through the GitHub MCP Registry in VS Code.

cons.text: The Copilot MCP route described here requires VS Code 1.99 or later, and Business or Enterprise organizations must enable the relevant policy.
The products document different setup and approval paths; verify each tool against the team’s editor, server and policy requirements.

faqs.question: Does the Copilot MCP policy apply to every account?
faqs.answer: No. GitHub scopes this policy to organization or enterprise users on Business or Enterprise; it does not govern individual Free, Pro, Pro+ or Max plans.

faqs.question: Can both connect to a local MCP server?
faqs.answer: The cited docs describe local stdio for Cursor and manual MCP server configuration for Copilot in VS Code. Confirm the exact server transport supported by your chosen client and version.

faqs.question: What does Cursor Privacy Mode cover, and what should an account verify?
faqs.answer: Cursor says Privacy Mode prevents training on Customer Data and that most model requests use provider zero-data-retention agreements, subject to safety and abuse review and non-ZDR model exceptions. Requests made with personal API keys still pass through Cursor's backend and rely on the provider's terms for retention. Optional Cloud Agents store encrypted repository copies while a run is active, then delete them after completion. Teams and Enterprise can enforce Privacy Mode; Cursor says individual plans follow its Privacy Policy rather than the commercial DPA. Verify the account setting, organization policy, model approvals, API-key route, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement; none was inspected here. Cursor also says Privacy Mode applies to Self-Hosted Machines and that code sent by the worker is not used for training when enabled, although run content still reaches Cursor and artifacts may upload to its storage; confirm whether this feature and setting apply to the account.

faqs.question: Can GitHub Copilot use locally run models?
faqs.answer: GitHub lists Local BYOK in VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and Copilot SDK. The client-side mechanism stores keys locally and removes dependence on the Copilot API. For Copilot CLI specifically, GitHub lists Ollama, vLLM and Foundry Local-compatible endpoints and requires tool calling and streaming. Offline mode prevents GitHub contact, but prompts and code context still reach a remote provider. Business/Enterprise organization policy can disable Local BYOK in IDEs. Confirm the client, policy and provider route; no account or model was tested.

faqs.question: Is Cursor Self-Hosted Machines equivalent to Copilot Local BYOK?
faqs.answer: No. Cursor Self-Hosted Machines move Cloud Agent tool calls to customer-managed workers while inference stays in Cursor cloud. Copilot Local BYOK is a client-side provider route in the documented supported clients; it is a different capability and does not imply that Cursor worker inference is local. Verify the exact client, plan and organization policy.
